terms.meaning: request for proposal, the document a client issues to ask for bids
a number for how close two pieces of text are, where lower means closer here
a piece of a document stored for search
a simple Python record type that stores named fields

depends_on: src/rag_engine.py (the RAG engine object passed in)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module setup
sections.what: Loads the typing, file path and record helpers, and describes the module's job.
sections.why: Needed for the record type and file names.

sections.name: RFPMatch
sections.title: Match result record
sections.what: Defines the record that holds the matched file name, its score, how many pieces matched, and the top snippets.
sections.why: Gives the rest of the program one standard result shape.

sections.name: RFPMatcher (part 1)
sections.title: Setup and search for similar RFPs
sections.what: Stores the RAG engine and runs the search on the first 2000 characters of the new RFP. It asks for five times the requested number of results so there is enough to group.
sections.why: Likely reason: more results give a fuller picture per file before averaging.
sections.watch_out: Only the first 2000 characters are used, so later requirements do not affect the match.

sections.name: RFPMatcher (part 2)
sections.title: Ranking RFPs by average score
sections.what: Groups results by source file, averages each file's scores, sorts so the lowest (closest) comes first, and returns the best one. Alternatives are printed when verbose.
sections.why: Averaging gives one number per file to compare.
sections.watch_out: A file with a single strong match can outrank a file with many good matches, because only the average is compared.

sections.name: RFPMatcher: extract_rfp_name
sections.title: Turning a file name into a base name
sections.what: Removes the file extension and common RFP suffixes such as _RFP from a file name, returning a short base name such as a client name.
sections.why: Likely reason: templates are named by client, so the file name must be cleaned to match.
sections.watch_out: The suffix is removed wherever it appears in the name, not only at the end.

summary: Finds which past RFP in the database is most similar to a new RFP, so that RFP's proposal can serve as the template.
purpose: Pick the closest historical RFP automatically.
why: The module docstring states it determines which proposal template to use.
how: Take the first 2000 characters of the new RFP, search stored RFP pieces, group results by source file, average each file's scores, and pick the file with the lowest average.
inputs: The new RFP's text and a number of alternatives to show.
outputs: A match record with the file name, average similarity score, number of matching pieces and top snippets. Returns nothing when no RFPs are stored.
risks: Averages ignore how many pieces matched. Only the first 2000 characters are used. The return type says RFPMatch but None is returned when nothing is found, so callers must check.
debug: Confirm that RFPs are indexed. Read the printed alternatives and scores. If the wrong file wins, compare match counts and consider the opening text used.
